title: Time as a Relational Evolution Parameter: A Unified Framework for Composite Quantum Mechanics, Measurement, the Born Rule, Bell Correlations, and Internal Standard Model Symmetries
content: This work continues the framework developed in Ref. [1], in which time is treated relationally as the +1 evolution parameter associated with the dimensional configuration space of a physical phenomenon, and quantum-mechanical structure is proposed to emerge from the information-preserving dimensional recording of a higher-dimensional wave field. Here we extend that construction beyond the single-system description and investigate whether additional central elements of quantum mechanics can arise without being introduced as independent quantum postulates. We first clarify the recording process in terms of physically distinguishable equivalence classes of parent configurations and show how changes of the parent field can produce effective measurement-induced state updating in the reduced description. For independently preparable systems, preservation of local linear superposition leads to bilinear composition and, subject to completeness of the accessible composite state space, to Hilbert-space tensor products. Joint interactions then generate nonfactorizable reduced states, providing a structural origin for entanglement before any probabilistic interpretation is introduced. We subsequently derive the Born probability rule from the geometry of orthogonal reduced alternatives together with unitary invariance, noncontextual consistency, continuity, normalization, and additive coarse-graining. The resulting probability structure is compared with the independent robustness-based reconstruction of De Raedt, Katsnelson, and Michielsen [2]. Using the derived composite structure and probability rule, Bell–CHSH correlations are obtained from generic interaction-generated pure entangled states without assuming a singlet state or Pauli spin operators, while operational no-signalling is preserved. Finally, we explore a possible geometric extension toward internal gauge symmetries: aligned three-dimensional, tilted three-dimensional, and fully four-dimensional parent-field deformations lead respectively to one, two, and three component complex internal representations, suggesting U(1), SU(2), and SU(3) type symmetry structures. Unlike approaches that take the quantum formalism as their starting point, or reconstruction programs based primarily on operational or informational axioms, the present framework seeks a concrete physical mechanism from which these structures emerge together. The fact that a single modification in the dimensional role of time, combined with information-preserving reduction, consistently generates multiple otherwise independent features of quantum theory makes this possibility physically significant even before genuinely new empirical predictions are established.
